name: hardstyle
title: Hardstyle
description: Four-on-the-floor dance music built around a distorted, pitched kick, with big minor-key lead melodies (euphoric) or darker screech-driven drops (raw).

structure.description: DJ-friendly: kick, hi-hats and percussion; hint the lead or a filtered motif in the second half.
Kick drops out; pads or a piano introduce the chord progression.
The melody in full over the chords, often with a vocal; no kick.
Snare or kick roll speeding up, rising filter and pitch; a short gap (one beat to one bar) before the drop.
Kick back on every beat under the main lead melody; in raw styles an anti-climax of rhythmic screeches over the kick.
Short breather reusing the breakdown melody.
Shorter, more intense build than the first.
Main melody again, often with variations or an extra layer.
Kick and percussion only, for mixing out.

rhythms.name: four on the floor
rhythms.description: Kick on every beat, the backbone of every section with drums.

rhythms.name: reverse bass
rhythms.description: Two bass 16ths after each kick (kick-bass-bass). Used in older and 'reverse bass' styles; modern tracks usually let the kick tail be the bass instead.

rhythms.name: clap on two and four
rhythms.description: Clap layered on beats 2 and 4, common in intros and climaxes.

rhythms.name: kick roll into the drop
rhythms.description: Four-bar roll getting denser before the drop; music_roll with a velocity ramp is the flexible way to write it.

rhythms.name: syncopated lead
rhythms.description: 3-3-2 lead rhythm (tresillo feel) that sits against the straight kick.

progressions.description: The major V pulls strongly back to the tonic; good for the end of a phrase.
Rising into the tonic, useful for the last phrase of a breakdown.
Dark flat-2 movement for raw drops, all chords within the scale.

guidance: The kick is the centrepiece: keep it on every beat whenever drums play, and keep other sounds out of its low end. Its tail is pitched, so tune it to the key's root (fl_set_step_params pitch on the kick channel).
In climaxes the kick tail often follows the chord roots, one pitch per bar or half bar.
Work in phrases of 8, 16 or 32 bars and change something at every phrase boundary; mark the last bar of a phrase with a fill or kick roll.
Leads are wide and layered: repeat the melody an octave up for the climax, and use slide or porta on notes for pitch glides.
Euphoric: emotional minor-key melodies, long breakdowns with pads or piano. Raw: darker scales (phrygian), screeches and distorted, rhythmic leads.
The breakdown melody usually returns in the climax, faster-feeling and louder, over the kick.
